question.text: An investment of Rs. 50,000 grows to Rs. 85,000 over 5 years. The Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) is closest to:

explanation.text: The Logic: CAGR = (End Value / Beginning Value)^(1/n) - 1 = (85,000/50,000)^(1/5) - 1 = (1.7)^(0.2) - 1 = 1.1120 - 1 = 11.20%. The Trap: Simple return would be (85,000 - 50,000)/50,000 = 70% over 5 years = 14% per year. But CAGR accounts for compounding and is lower. 12.50% and 10.80% are nearby distractors. Note: Removed the "Rs." currency prefix from the 14.00% option so it reads as a clean percentage, and dropped distributor/cross-exam framing.
